title: SMTO-EML-0004 — SMTO couldn't open a secure connection to your mail server
summary: SMTO tried to open an encrypted connection to your mail server, but the server didn't offer one or its security certificate couldn't be trusted. SMTO stopped before sending, so no email went out.

headings.title: SMTO-EML-0004 — SMTO couldn't open a secure connection to your mail server

html:
SMTO-EML-0004 — SMTO couldn't open a secure connection to your mail server

GUID: 8114c589-2925-5dd1-85ef-03c3729bd5e0
Slug: email-starttls-unavailable
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open an encrypted connection to your mail server, but the server didn't offer one or its security certificate couldn't be trusted. SMTO stopped before sending, so no email went out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu, select your email sender profile, and check the server name and port match your email provider's settings. Port 587 normally uses starttls; port 465 uses implicit_tls. A port paired with the wrong security mode is the most common reason the encrypted connection fails.
  2. Make sure the server name is the full name your provider gives (for example smtp.office365.com), not a nickname or a different address. SMTO checks that the server's certificate matches that name and refuses the connection if it doesn't.
  3. If your organization runs its own mail server with its own certificates, ask your IT team for their certificate and have it added to the sender profile as a custom certificate. Without it, SMTO can't confirm a privately issued certificate is genuine.
  4. Ask SMTO in a conversation to test the email connection for that sender profile. The test checks the secure connection without sending any email.

What success looks like

  • The connection test reports the mail server is ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your mail server or SMTO. Don't turn off certificate checks (the insecure option); that would let someone intercept your email and password.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's SMTP client could not establish TLS: STARTTLS was required but not advertised, or the TLS handshake or certificate verification failed before any message data was sent.

What this means

  • SMTP lacks required STARTTLS support or raises TLS certificate/handshake errors before message transmission becomes uncertain. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • SMTP lacks required STARTTLS support or raises TLS certificate/handshake errors before message transmission becomes uncertain.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect STARTTLS advertisement, TLS mode, server hostname and CA verification evidence.

How to fix it

  • Verify server, port and tls.mode in the email_smtp profile against the provider (STARTTLS usually on 587, implicit TLS on 465); STARTTLS never falls back to plaintext. For verification failures confirm the server name matches the certificate, and for a private CA set tls.verification to custom_ca with a valid tls.ca_pem; test from the Gateway host, for example openssl s_client -starttls smtp -connect host:587 -servername host.
  • Check server TLS mode, hostname and CA trust. STARTTLS never falls back to plaintext.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended SMTP endpoint completes verified TLS without plaintext fallback.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
